name: no-organiser-named-act-pursued
rule: A listing that names no producing organisation is researched through the people it DOES name (#1856). The show is billed as a TITLE, so the act's names live only in the listing text the app rendered; the run reads that, pursues the named leads, and never labels anyone `presenter`, because the only organisation on the page is the room.

sources.content: Delaney Brown is a singer and actor based in New York. She hosts Broadway's Bad Guys! at The Example Room on August 14 with Miggie Snyder. Booking and general enquiries: delaney@delaneybrown.example.

sources.content: Miggie Snyder is a performer and music director in New York. Upcoming: Broadway's Bad Guys! at The Example Room, August 14. Get in touch: miggie@miggiesnyder.example.

sources.label: The Example Room listing host
sources.content: The Example Room is a rental cabaret room. Ticketing questions: tickets@theexampleroom.example. To perform here: programming@theexampleroom.example.

expected.description: The show title is not an organisation, so hunting for one and reporting that nobody publishes an address is the failure this fixture exists to catch. Both hosts named in the listing text are pursued directly, each with their own second-person body. The room's two inboxes are refused, and nothing is labelled `presenter`: no producer was ever established. The summary term is the STEM, because the expectation is that the run said what the show is, not that it happened to pluralise the word the way this fixture's author did: a real run on 2026-07-31 wrote "musical theatre villain songs", a correct answer that an exact match on "villains" scored as a failure.

results.showSummary: A cabaret evening of musical theatre villain songs hosted by two performers, 70 minutes, 16+.

draft.subject: Photographing Broadway's Bad Guys! at The Example Room
draft.body: My name is Dan and I'm a professional arts photographer here in NYC. I'm writing in regard to Broadway's Bad Guys! at The Example Room on August 14. I shoot unobtrusive, no-flash documentary coverage, so the audience doesn't notice me and the performance isn't disturbed. I've been photographing at Carnegie Hall for close to ten years, and you can see my portfolio at danwrightphotography.com. If you don't have someone on it already, I'd be glad to talk about your photography plans for the night. I look forward to hearing from you.
